findings.probable_cause_of_the_false_report: news-scout's cycle ran 16:09-16:17Z and spans the mcp-server restart at 16:10:02Z (docker inspect StartedAt=2026-07-21T16:10:02.506Z). news-scout itself logged 'one transient gateway EOF on host.docker.internal:3000/sse, recovered on retry'. A transport failure during that restart was almost certainly misread as a tool-contract rejection. UNPROVEN as the specific mechanism — stated as probable cause, not fact.

That call is CORRECT per the tool contract — no change needed. Recorded so a fixer does not 'fix' a working call site.
news-scout's separate claim that agent:'all' returned #8677 and #8679 but MISSED #8678 was NOT verified by cowork-team. Untested. Do not treat as established.

OPEN QUESTION, NOT A FINDING: the live from_agent=null call returned 94 rows for a 0.25h window, all alert-engine VERIFIED_DECISION, carrying expires_at stamps HOURS in the past (04:00, 10:30, 15:45) — an expiry preceding creation does not reconcile with a created_at-bounded window. The query reads correct, so cowork-team is NOT calling this a bug. Worth exactly one look by whoever owns agent_signals.
findings.requested_action: Before triaging news-scout-20260721T161414Z.json finding #1: re-read it against this correction. Recommend closing its HIGH as NOT-A-DEFECT (infra-transient misattribution) and instead minting a much smaller doc/robustness item — the flow's documented non-fatal branch converts a transport failure into a silently-empty dedup cache, which is the real hazard and is a different bug from the one reported.

findings.title: cowork-team parallel fan-out has no producer/consumer ordering — alert-commander reads the signal bus before its producers write to it
findings.mechanism: BGFAN-1 mandates run_in_background=true for every dispatcher spawn and spawn-fanout.md issues all matched slots in ONE parallel block. There is no dependency ordering. When a tick matches both a PRODUCER (market-watcher -> posts price_anomaly; news-scout -> posts urgent_news/chain_catalyst) and a CONSUMER (alert-commander -> gates on those exact signal types), the consumer can complete its bus read before the producers have posted.

evidence_16_00Z_tick.consumer_observation: alert-commander ran ~16:10-16:15Z and reported: 'zero verified_chain/chain_catalyst/price_anomaly on the bus (verified by explicit signal_type-filtered calls, not just the general one)'. Its evidence was CLEAN — the bus genuinely was empty at read time.
evidence_16_00Z_tick.producer_observation: market-watcher-offhours posted price_anomaly signal 8680 (GAS -6.98%, 2.89 sigma, 4.02x volume) and 8681 (D2D -3.30%, 52-week low) at ~16:17Z — AFTER alert-commander had already exited silent.
evidence_16_00Z_tick.consequence: alert-commander's position-danger gate failed at condition 1/3 for want of price signals that its sibling produced two minutes later, on a session with real >5% drops (GAS -6.98%, BSR -6.49%, GEX -5.16%). The silent exit was CORRECT given what it could see; the dispatch order is what made it blind.

findings.important_scoping: This does NOT establish that get_alerts(type='price') is broken. alert-commander separately reported get_alerts(type='price') empty; prior art FIX-ALERT-SCAN-REJECT-STUB-BAR-P0 and FIX-ALERT-OPEN-ZERO-PRICE-RACE sit in that neighbourhood and were NOT re-filed. At least part of this cycle's blindness is dispatcher ordering, not detector failure. Both causes may be live; do not let one absorb the other.
findings.related_second_order_effect: Same tick, R3 (match-slots.md Step 4b: multi-slot collision WARNs but never blocks) spawned market-watcher twice. market-watcher-offhours reported the consequence: the EOD slot fired late (~16:08-16:13Z) which pushed the 16:09 dispatch into offhours, so TWO market-watcher cycles processed the SAME 08:32 closing prices four minutes apart. Duplicated work per close. R3 is working as written; the written rule is what needs review.
findings.requested_action: Design decision for agents-architect: either (a) order the fan-out into producer-wave then consumer-wave within a tick, (b) have consumers re-read the bus after a bounded wait when co-dispatched producers are known to be in flight, or (c) accept and document that consumers lag producers by one tick. cowork-team has NOT implemented any of these — dispatcher must not self-modify its own contract.
